subject: SyncData: Trial → Prod commitment plan, PO & invoicing cadence
summary: Initial MAP + commercial terms for SyncData evaluation and production ramp. Key asks: confirm PO process, Net30 vs Net60, invoicing cadence (one-time onboarding + monthly), billing start tied to production cutover. Proposed discounts contingent on term and committed ramp.
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@syncdata.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.p@syncdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: SyncData: Trial → Prod commitment plan & invoicing ask

Hi Elena / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised I'm sharing a concise Mutual Action Plan (attached) that maps the evaluation gates to commercial milestones and the invoicing flow we typically follow. High level:

- Pilot / evaluation (2 weeks): Smoke tests, latency SLA checks, 1 sample endpoint + security review. No charge for evaluation tokens up to the pilot cap in MAP.
- Accept / cutover: Once your engineering sign-off is done we move to production.
- Ramp window (months 1–3): Target 100k tokens/day by month 2, steady-state thereafter.

Commercial outline (proposal):
- Pricing: tiered per-token pricing (see MAP doc).
- Discount: 20% off list with a 12-month committed minimum. 10% for a 6-month commit.
- Payment terms: Standard is Net30. We can consider Net60 for enterprise procurements with an approved PO and credit approval.
- Invoicing cadence: One-time onboarding fee invoiced at signature; recurring usage invoiced monthly in arrears.
- PO requirement: We require a purchase order on file before we start billing. PO can be uploaded to the HubSpot record or sent to procurement@redwood.com.
- Billing start date: Prefer to start billing on production cutover (the date we flip DNS / live traffic). If you need billing to align differently, tell us and we can set a graceful start date in the agreement (e.g., 30 days after go-live).

Attached: SyncData-MAP-v1.pdf, PO_Template_SyncData.xlsx, sample-invoice-Redwood-202611.pdf.

Action items for SyncData: please confirm procurement email for PO submission, preferred payment terms (Net30 vs Net60), and whether the 12-month commit / discount is acceptable. If Net60 is required, let us know and we'll route for approvals.

Target timeline to keep to: PO + signed MAP by 2026-11-21 to allow a 2026-12-01 billing start if cutover is on schedule.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Martinez <elena@syncdata.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.p@syncdata.com>, procurement@syncdata.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SyncData: Trial → Prod commitment plan & invoicing ask

Diego —

Appreciate the clear MAP. A few notes from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement preference: Net60 is our standard for new SaaS vendors. We can escalate to Net30 if needed, but it requires legal signoff and payment team approval.
- Invoicing: We prefer staged invoices — one onboarding invoice at signature (fine), then monthly usage invoices. Is there any flexibility to pro-rate the first month if cutover happens mid-month?
- Billing start: We agree billing should begin on production cutover. If there is a delay on our side, we expect billing to be pushed to the agreed start date.
- Discounts: Curious whether the 20% discount can be applied pro-rata to the first monthly invoice once commit is signed, or whether it must be applied from invoice following the commit effective date.

Looping in procurement (procurement@syncdata.com) — please advise on internal PO timeline.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Product, SyncData

Diego / team — quick internal note for how we should respond:

- Net60: we can approve Net60 for SyncData on the condition of an approved PO (no exceptions) and a 9-month minimum commitment. That gives us cashflow predictability while respecting their AR cycles.
- Discount mechanics: offer the 20% discount if SyncData signs a 12-month commitment. If they sign 6 months, apply 10% immediately. For a 9-month concession (to get Net60), we can offer 15% as a middle ground.
- Invoicing cadence: onboarding fee at signature (one-time). Usage billed monthly in arrears. We can pro-rate the first month if cutover is mid-month — standard practice.
- Billing start: Must be explicitly defined in the MAP: "billing start = production cutover date unless a written delay agreement is provided by customer." If they request billing to start later, it must be in writing and include an agreed fallback date.

I recommend we propose: Net60 accepted with 9-month minimum + 15% discount, or Net30 with 12-month + 20% discount. Ben to approve final concession once Elena confirms procurement timeline.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Sales — Redwood Inference

Elena / Rajiv / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses and context. Based on the team's guidance above, here is the suggested commercial path we can document in the MAP (I'll attach an updated PDF and the revised invoice schedule):

1) Payment terms and PO
- We can accept Net60 for SyncData provided we receive a formal PO before we begin billing and the customer signs a 9-month minimum commitment.
- Alternative: Net30 if SyncData signs a 12-month commitment (20% discount).

2) Discounts
- 12-month term → 20% discount (applies from the first invoice following effective date).
- 9-month term (Net60 concession) → 15% discount (applies from the first invoice following effective date).
- 6-month term → 10% discount.

3) Invoicing cadence
- Onboarding fee invoiced at signature (one-time).
- Usage invoiced monthly in arrears. We will pro-rate the first usage invoice if cutover is mid-month.

4) Billing start date
- By default, billing starts on production cutover (the day we flip live traffic). If SyncData requests a deferred start date, we require a written confirmation with an explicit fallback date (no later than 30 days after originally scheduled cutover).

Next steps:
- Please confirm which commercial path you prefer (Net60 + 9 months, Net30 + 12 months, or Net30/Net60 + 6 months).
- Procurement: if possible, provide estimated PO issue date (we're targeting PO + signed MAP by 2026-11-21 to align a 2026-12-01 billing start).

I'll attach an updated MAP and revised invoice schedule for signature. If everything looks good I can send the DocuSign this week.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
